title: Version-anchor automated probe dispatcher for catalog and tenant-locked models
creator: Marina Ortega
description: Design and ship a dispatcher service that automatically triggers targeted evaluation probes when a model version is anchored in the catalog or when a tenant upgrades/locks a model. The dispatcher should support cost-aware sampling, tenant-priority overrides, and configurable probe profiles so we can run lightweight smoke checks for low-risk changes and more comprehensive regressions for major upgrades. This ticket focuses on the product requirements, sampling policies, and rollout plan; engineering tickets will follow for runtime implementation and infra hardening.
background_and_problem_statement: Customers and catalog maintainers sometimes promote new model builds or change serving configs; without automated, targeted checks we risk silent quality regressions (hallucinations, formatting regressions, prompt-sensitivity) reaching production. Current eval workflows are manual or broad-sampled and either miss tenant-specific regressions or blow evaluation budgets. We need a dispatcher that: identifies anchor/lock events, maps them to probe suites, schedules probes across tenant segments, enforces cost caps, and exposes evaluation results to Console and alerting pipelines.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a version-anchor probe dispatcher that listens to catalog events (catalog lock/anchor, model revision publish) and tenant model-lock events. For each event it will: (1) compute a probe profile (quick smoke, medium fidelity, or full regression) using change heuristics; (2) determine sampling policy (tenant-aware sampling, 100% for high-impact tenants, probabilistic otherwise); (3) allocate budgeted compute tokens and schedule probes into the eval worker pool; (4) publish results to the eval results topic and surface failures to Console and the regression-watcher alerting pipeline. Include configuration for budget caps, emergency full-replays, and manual-trigger API for on-demand replays.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher accepts catalog anchor events and tenant lock/upgrade events and creates evaluation jobs in the eval queue
Probe profiles (smoke/medium/full) selected based on change heuristics documented in the policy table
Sampling honors tenant-priority overrides and respects per-tenant monthly eval budget caps
Failed probes for production-impacting signals generate a regression alert and create a linked incident in PagerDuty or create regression ticket draft
Console shows a per-event evaluation summary (pass/fail, key metrics, token cost) and links to detailed result artifacts
Manual re-run endpoint exists for customers and internal SRE with audit logging
acceptance_test_plan: Unit tests for event-to-profile mapping logic
Integration test: simulate catalog anchor -> jobs enqueued -> results posted to topic
Canary: enable dispatcher for a single low-volume tenant and verify sampling + budget enforcement over 48h
Cost regression check: compare token spend against baseline for similar past anchors
User acceptance: Console shows evaluation summaries and PM/SE confirms the alerting workflow for a mock regression
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: How aggressive should automatic replays be for minor config diffs? (we propose conservative default: smoke-only for config-only diffs)
Edge-case: model architecture-only metadata changes — will probe profile be stale? Need a classifier to detect semantic weight of a change
Budget enforcement granularity: monthly tenant cap vs per-event cap (propose both; per-event multiplier configurable)
Integration with Dedicated/private deployments where eval infra may be restricted — should dispatch a lightweight shadow-run instead of full probe?
Operational cost: extra eval traffic could spike during major catalog promotions; we need throttling and backoff tied to cluster utilization
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement dispatcher with smoke-only profile and enable for internal catalog promotions; monitoring and manual kill switch
Phase 2 (canary): enable tenant-aware sampling for 5 beta customers with explicit consent; collect cost and false-positive rates
Phase 3 (gradual): default enable for public catalog anchors and allow customers to opt-out or adjust budgets from Console
Phase 4 (GA): expose advanced probe configuration and tenant-priority matrix to account admins and integrate with automated rollback playbooks
observability_and_metrics: Jobs enqueued / jobs completed per event
Median time from anchor event -> evaluation summary published
Token consumption per event and aggregated per tenant
False positive rate of regression alerts (post-moderation)
ui_and_console_changes: New Catalog event timeline card showing evaluation status and quick-replay button
Tenant settings page: eval budget slider and opt-out toggle
Evaluation detail panel with pass/fail, top-delta-metrics, and link to full artifact storage
Rollout/upgrade preview screen to simulate expected probe profile and estimated token cost
security_and_compliance_considerations: Probes running against customer prompts must not leak tenant data in aggregated public metrics
Store eval artifacts in tenant-scoped S3 buckets with KMS encryption matching tenant configuration
Audit logs for manual triggers and replays must be retained per compliance retention policy
Private deployments: dispatcher should publish only metadata to control plane; raw probe payloads must remain in-customer network when required
notes: Spike completed by ENG on 2026-02-20 demonstrated <10% extra token spend for smoke-first strategy (see spike doc)
We will reuse existing eval worker pool and add lightweight priority queue to avoid head-of-line blocking for scheduled customer traffic
Initial probe profile mapping heuristics drafted in doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/anchor-dispatcher-profiles
